original_value: The automatic diagnosis has been suffering from the problem of inadequate reliable corpus to train a trustworthy predictive model. Besides, most of the previous deep learning based diagnosis models adopt the sequence learning techniques (CNN or RNN), which is difficult to extract the complex structural information, e.g. graph structure, between the critical medical entities. In this paper, we propose to build the diagnosis model based on the high-standard EMR documents from real hospitals to improve the accuracy and the credibility of the resulting model. Meanwhile, we introduce the Graph Convolutional Network into the model that alleviates the sparse feature problem and facilitates the extraction of structural information for diagnosis. Moreover, we propose the mutual attentive network to enhance the representation of inputs towards the better model performance. The evaluation conducted on the real EMR documents demonstrates that the proposed model is more accurate compared to the previous sequence learning based diagnosis models. The proposed model has been integrated into the information systems in over hundreds of primary health care facilities in China to assist physicians in the diagnostic process.

result.paraphrase: Automatic diagnosis has long been hindered by a lack of dependable training corpora for building trustworthy predictive models. In addition, most prior deep learning–based diagnosis models rely on sequence-learning methods such as CNNs or RNNs, which struggle to capture complex structural relations, such as graph structure, among key medical entities. In this paper, we propose constructing the diagnosis model from high-quality EMR documents collected from real hospitals, with the goal of improving the accuracy and credibility of the resulting model. At the same time, we incorporate a Graph Convolutional Network to mitigate sparse feature issues and better extract structural information for diagnosis. We also introduce a mutual attentive network to strengthen input representations and further improve model performance. Evaluation on real EMR documents shows that the proposed model is more accurate than earlier sequence-learning-based diagnosis models. The model has been integrated into information systems at more than hundreds of primary health care facilities in China to support physicians in the diagnostic process.
